podcast.title: Early 2000s Revival (2000-2001)
podcast.body: The early 2000s saw a significant "Indie Rock Revival," or "Post-Punk Revival," which was essentially a refurbished version of the old-school early alt rock from the late 1980s. This style itself was a repeat of 1960s garage rock fused with mid-1970s punk. "The first happened around 2000 and 2001, when Indie Rock, which really was a refurbished version of the old-school early alt rock of the late 80s, which itself was a repeat of the garage rock of the late 60s, made it with a punk in the mid 1970s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 2: (90-81)

podcast.title: Revolution and Resurgence (2000-2004)
podcast.body: The period between 2000 and 2004 saw an "Indie Rock Revolution" and a subsequent resurgence of all things rock. During this time, the rock world continued the habit of making music videos, as exemplified by bands like Queens of the Stone Age, who used clips like "No One Knows" to gain attention. "And the rock world was still in the habit of making videos, especially around 2000 to 2004, during the Indie Rock Revolution and the subsequent resurgence of all things rock at that time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Future of the Music Video - Part 2

podcast.title: Chart Dominance (End of 2005)
podcast.body: By the end of 2005, the interest in indie music had grown substantially, to the extent that all top 10 records on the charts could be classified as indie, demonstrating its significant commercial and cultural impact. "if you looked at the charts from the end of 2005, you could classify all top 10 records on that chart as indie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of Indie Rock: Part 4

podcast.title: Golden Age in Hamilton (circa 2006)
podcast.body: The mid-2000s, specifically around 2006, was described as the "Golden Age" of indie rock in Hamilton. During this period, numerous prominent indie bands and artists like Winter Sleep, Joel Plaskett, Constantine's, Stars, Sam Roberts, and Arcade Fire regularly played at local clubs such as The Casbah and The Underground, creating a vibrant music scene. "It was also at the height of the kind of like Indy Rock era, the Golden Age I'd say. You know, so every week at the club it seemed like at the Casbore, the Underground there was bands like Winner Sleep or Joel Plasket, Constantine, Stars, Sam Roberts, Arcade for all of these bands just coming through Hamilton that we got to go."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Arkells - In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: 21st Century Revival and Cheap Instruments
podcast.body: The 21st century saw an "indie revival" characterized by numerous guitar-based bands. Many of these bands consciously chose to use cheap instruments, such as those favored by The White Stripes, Yeah Yeah Yeahs, The Strokes, and The Black Keys, as part of their anti-establishment image, shunning expensive vintage gear. "Then the 21st century began with the indie revival with dozens and dozens of guitar based bands, many choosing to use cheap instruments as part of their anti-establishment image."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Story of the Electric Guitar - Part 3

podcast.title: Aesthetics Compared to Hip Hop
podcast.body: Indie attitudes are distinct from hip-hop; for example, an indie band would not typically sing about luxury items like "drinking crystal in the back of a maybok" or "diamonds and their new grills." "Compare indie attitudes with hip hop. Now an indie band wouldn't think about singing about drinking crystal in the back of a maybok, well, discussing the size of the diamonds and their new grills."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Diversity Show 2021

podcast.title: American 80s Scene
podcast.body: American 80s indie rock was a broad category encompassing various bands such as Sonic Youth, Pixies, and Dinosaur Jr., representing the diverse rock movements of the period. "lo que muchas veces agrupamos el in-derroque de los 80 americanos, que junta de todo, junta a sol y lluz, junta a los píxis, a dainers or junior."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cuál fue el primer disco de Grunge?

podcast.title: Birth in North America
podcast.body: North American indie rock is a key subject of "Chapter 8" in the history of Alt Rock. It refers to the independent rock scene that developed across the continent, often in regional enclaves. "The birth of North American indie rock and the first use of the word alternative."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 8

podcast.title: Defining Characteristics
podcast.body: The indie universe encompasses the underground, the non-mainstream, the experimental, the daring, the outliers, the unusual, and the non-conformist. It represents music that is often "not ready for prime time" in the mainstream. "This is the universe of the underground, the non-mainstream, the experimental, the daring, the outliers, the unusual, the non-conformist."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 2

podcast.title: Definition and Origins
podcast.body: "Indie" music is defined by artists who operate independently from major record labels, often self-producing or even launching their own labels. This movement saw early examples like the Buzzcocks and was fostered by small independent labels working outside the major system. "Now indie, as far as we're concerned, means artists who have done everything on their own with no help, that is independent from one of the big established record labels."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 7: All the rest

podcast.title: Digital World's Influence
podcast.body: The Indie Rock Revival of the early 2000s served as one of the earliest and most prominent examples of how the nascent "new digital world" could effectively generate and sustain a novel musical movement. The ease of illegal file-sharing platforms like Napster enabled listeners to effortlessly discover and access new bands, circumventing traditional record store searches and contributing to the genre's organic rise and widespread appeal. "The indie rock revival was one of the very first examples of how the new digital world could produce and sustain a brand new musical movement and trend."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 9: (20-11)

podcast.title: Early 2000s Revival
podcast.body: The early 2000s witnessed a significant "Indie Rock Revival," a broad cultural movement spanning North America and parts of Europe that brought about a resurgence of "stripped down guitar-based rock." This movement was crucial because, by the end of the 1990s, guitar rock was widely considered "dead," with electronica predicted to dominate music. Bands, many originating from New York (The Strokes, Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Interpol, TV on the Radio), Detroit (The White Stripes), Sweden (The Hives), England (The Libertines), and Scotland (Franz Ferdinand), spearheaded this revival, initially operating underground before their music gained traction on radio, TV, films, and commercials, and at festivals like Coachella and Glastonbury. "This was important because at the end of the 1990s, it did look like guitar rock was dead. It was all about electronica."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 9: (20-11)

podcast.title: Early 2000s Revival Context
podcast.body: The early 2000s saw a significant revival of indie rock, with bands like Arctic Monkeys, Franz Ferdinand, Interpol, Block Party, and The Strokes emerging. Many of these bands initially stayed within a predictable and solid musical trajectory, gradually improving their style but often reluctant to leave their comfort zones. "Todas estas bandas que salían a primeros del 2000, en este rival del Rock, el que formaban parte de los Artic Monkeys."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: ARCTIC MONKEYS - Tranquility Base Hotel & Casino. Por qué tiene más sentido del que parece

podcast.title: Early 2000s Revival Wave
podcast.body: Sum 41 also positioned itself at the beginning of the indie rock revival in the early 2000s, capitalizing on this burgeoning scene to achieve rapid international recognition. "in the beginning of this whole indie rock revival in the early 2000."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Sum 41 Story As Told By Deryck Whibley: Part 1

podcast.title: Early Classic - Pere Ubu's "Final Solution"
podcast.body: Pere Ubu's 1976 song "Final Solution," the third song they ever recorded, became recognized as an "indie rock classic," showcasing their self-produced and experimental approach to music. "This has become something of an indie rock classic."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 3

podcast.title: Engine of Change
podcast.body: Indie rock is described as the engine of change for rock and roll, where all forthcoming sounds, trends, and fads originate. Its work and art drag listeners into the future. "The indie universe is the engine of change for rock and roll. Whatever sounds and trends and fads are coming next start here."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 2

podcast.title: Equivalence to Alternative Music
podcast.body: By the mid-1980s, indie music in the UK was pushing its weight around and for all intents and purposes was considered the same as what was called alternative music in North America. "By the middle 80s, indie music, which for all intents and purposes was the same as what we would call alternative music here in North America, was really pushing its weight around."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 2

podcast.title: Explosion in Post-Grunge Era
podcast.body: After a period where the grunge "well basically went dry" in the late 1990s, indie rock has "exploded" as alt-rock radio has moved away from its heavy reliance on grunge guitars. This has led to a much greater variety of sounds in alt-rock today.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Theories, Thoughts, and Half-Baked Ideas

podcast.title: Foundations in Early 2000s
podcast.body: The Strokes' debut album `Is This It` became one of the foundations for the indie rock movement that emerged later in the 2000s. "This is it album became one of the foundations for the indie rock movement that we'd see later in the decade."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 14

podcast.title: Grammy Recognition in the 2010s
podcast.body: By the 2010s, even Indie Rock seemed "venerable enough for the Grammys," particularly as an alternative to Rap and Dance Pop. This was exemplified by The Arcade Fire's unexpected Album of the Year win for "The Suburbs" in 2011. "By the 2010s, even Indy Rock seemed venerable enough for the Grammys, especially as an alternative to Rap and Dance Pop."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: And the Grammy Goes to… Edition Part 2

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: And the Grammy Goes to… Edition Part 2

podcast.title: Historical Perception
podcast.body: For decades, independent labels were commonly perceived as "minor leagues," with the attitude that any truly good or commercially viable music would inevitably be signed by a major label. Consequently, the world of Indie Rock was often seen as a place for "extra weird misfits" or artists whose talent was questioned, a characterization deemed "totally unfair" in most cases. "For decades, the attitude was that if you recorded for an independent label, you were in the minor leagues. The world of Indy Rock, which itself was a subset within the already left of center alternative rock scene, was a place to put all the extra weird misfits or those whose talent was questioned totally unfair. Mostly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of Indie Rock: Part 4

podcast.title: Increased Power and Credibility
podcast.body: Indie culture emerged as a powerful global force in the late 2000s, with an "indie" label becoming crucial for a musician's brand, appeal, and credibility. This was facilitated by the ability of small independent labels to rapidly capitalize on trends and bypass traditional gatekeepers. "Indie culture is now in fact a powerful force just about everywhere in the world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 15

podcast.title: Influence on General Rock Sound (2010s)
podcast.body: The sounds originating from various levels of indie rock directly contributed to the softer and more poppy overall sound of rock in the 2010s. "This was a direct result of the sounds percolating through all the different levels of indie rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Innovation and Risk-Taking
podcast.body: Despite facing skepticism, the indie world was a fertile ground where people were willing to take chances, which frequently led to the emergence of new sounds, trends, bands, or even just new songs, fostering innovation within the music industry. "this is also the universe where people took chances, and every once in a while, something great inevitably happened, a new sound, a new trend, a new band, or even just a new song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of Indie Rock: Part 4

podcast.title: Lofi Affiliation
podcast.body: In the late 1980s, the Lofi label was frequently affixed to many indie rock bands, especially those that ventured into a "Ram Shackle Territory" sound, even if they recorded in professional studios. "By the late 80s, the Lofi label was being affixed to many indie rock bands who occasionally veered into, let's call it, Ram Shackle Territory."

podcast.title: Misunderstood Term
podcast.body: "Indie Rock" or "Indie Music" is often misunderstood, with ten different people providing ten different definitions for the term. The term can refer to a sound, a business approach, a financial state, or an ephemeral aesthetic. "If there's one term that's misunderstood, it's Indy Rock or Indy Music. You ask 10 different people and you'll get 10 different definitions."

podcast.title: Modern Era in UK
podcast.body: The C86 cassette, released in 1986, is considered by some to be the beginning of the modern era of indie music in the UK, demonstrating a collective interest in independent music and inspiring an explosion of new bands. "In hindsight, some considered the release and subsequent success of this cassette to be the beginning of the modern era of indie music in the UK."

podcast.body: Indie rock, alongside rock and alt-rock, is widely perceived as predominantly white, leading to cultural discussions. "Rock, alt, rock and indie rock are predominantly white."

podcast.title: Response to Music Piracy
podcast.body: During the era of music piracy and illegal downloads, when the music establishment faced disruption, the indie world was compelled to step up and innovate, taking the lead in figuring out new operational models for the industry. "when things got weird with the music establishment and the era of music piracy and illegal downloads, it was the Indy world that was forced to step up and figure what everybody needed to do."

podcast.title: Revival Post 9/11
podcast.body: Indie rock experienced a revival in popularity after the 9/11 attacks and the American invasions of Iraq and Afghanistan. As happy music seemed inappropriate for the times, bands like The Strokes, The White Stripes, and The Killers contributed to a renewed interest in rock music. "This popularity began to rise again, driven by an indie rock revival."

podcast.title: Revival and Resilience (Late 90s - Early 2000s)
podcast.body: In the late 1990s and early 2000s, when guitar rock seemed grim due to the dominance of pop, hip-hop, and electronica, and the impact of internet file-sharing, indie rock not only survived but "brought everything back," initiating a revolution in the 21st century. "But indie rock survived. In fact, it brought everything back. Rock needed a shot in the arm, and once again, it was the indie world that provided it."

podcast.title: Revolution in Late 1990s and 2000s
podcast.body: An "indie rock revolution" began to take hold in the very late 1990s and subsequently "exploded" for the following decade, representing a new generation's effort to revitalize the genre. By the mid-2000s, the indie rock scene was rapidly growing in size, popularity, and influence. "a new generation of young people decided to take matters into their own hands and kickstart things themselves. We saw this with the indie rock revolution that started taking hold in the very late 1990s and then exploded for the next decade."

podcast.title: Rise in the 21st Century
podcast.body: Indie rock experienced a significant rise in the first decade of the 21st century, becoming a powerful force globally. Its growth was fueled by new technologies that leveled the playing field, allowing small independent companies to quickly distribute music worldwide without major label support. "the rise of Indy Rock in the first decade of the 21st century."
